q.t: Work done by a constant force = force × …
o: Displacement in the direction of the force
q.e: Only the displacement along the force counts.

q.t: The SI unit of work is the…

Gravitational potential energy near Earth = ?
q.e: Valid where g is nearly constant.

q.t: Does work have direction?
o: No — it is a signed number
q.e: Force and displacement have direction; work doesn't.

q.t: The capacity to do work is…
Energy stored in fuels and food is…
Energy stored because of deformation or position is…
q.e: A stretched band or a raised ball.

q.t: The joule is named after…
q.e: He related mechanical and thermal energy.

q.t: On a force–displacement graph, work done is the…
You hold a heavy bag still for 10 minutes. Work done on the bag is…
q.e: No displacement — though your muscles use internal energy.

q.t: Carrying a bag horizontally at constant velocity, work done by your upward force is…
A goalkeeper stopping a ball does ___ work on the ball.
q.e: Force opposite to the ball's displacement.

q.t: Work–energy theorem: net work done equals the change in…
Doubling velocity makes kinetic energy…
Moving an object horizontally changes its potential energy by…
A pendulum at its lowest point has maximum…
q.e: Potential is max at the ends.

q.t: Why does a real pendulum slowly stop?
o: Friction and air resistance remove mechanical energy
q.e: It goes into heat, not stored.

q.t: Speed at the bottom of a frictionless slide depends only on…
Is work done against friction stored as potential energy?
q.e: Only some internal forces store energy.

q.t: Why are energy methods often easier than Newton's laws?
o: Only start and end states matter
q.e: No need to track every slope.

q.t: A sand ramp stops runaway trucks by…
o: Friction removing energy and climbing converting KE to PE

q.t: Power is…

q.e: Always less than 100% due to friction.

o: Changing the size or direction of force

q.t: Can a machine give out more work than put in?
q.e: Less effort means a longer distance.

o: No external forces like friction act
